tooltip.title: Treatment Algorithm for Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown: Treatment is stratified based on disease severity (Body Surface Area affected) and location.

tooltip.title: Mild to Moderate Plaque Psoriasis (<5-10% BSA)
First-Line for Mild Psoriasis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **High-potency topical corticosteroids** (e.g., clobetasol).
-   Combination topicals (e.g., **steroid + vitamin D analog**) are often more effective.

tooltip.title: Second-Line & Special Sites
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Face/Flexures:** Lower potency steroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors.
-   **Refractory Plaques:** Topical retinoids (Tazarotene), intralesional steroid injections.

tooltip.title: Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis (>5-10% BSA or impacting sensitive areas)
Phototherapy
tooltip.markdown: An excellent option for patients with widespread disease who have access and no contraindications. **Narrowband UVB** is the preferred modality.

tooltip.title: Systemic Therapy
tooltip.markdown: The mainstay for most patients with moderate-to-severe disease.

tooltip.title: Biologics as First-Line Systemic
tooltip.markdown:
Due to their high efficacy and favorable safety profiles, biologics are often preferred. Choice depends on comorbidities and patient factors.

-   **IL-17 / IL-23 inhibitors:** Generally offer the highest levels of skin clearance (PASI 90/100).
-   **TNF-α inhibitors:** Broadly effective, especially if PsA is also present.

tooltip.title: Oral Systemics
tooltip.markdown:
Still important options.

-   **Methotrexate:** A cost-effective choice for skin and joints.
-   **Apremilast:** Oral option with a favorable safety profile (no lab monitoring).
-   **Deucravacitinib:** A newer oral selective TYK2 inhibitor with efficacy comparable to some biologics.
